name: Code & AI Security Audit — Prove Every Finding
summary: Audits a codebase and the AI agent that runs against it: attack-surface map, untrusted-input-to-sink tracing, leaked secrets, vulnerable dependencies, OWASP, tool/MCP permissions, prompt injection and spend caps. Every finding must be proven.
description:
Most security audits fail the same way: they list everything a scanner flags, bury the two things that will actually be exploited, and are ignored. This skill does the opposite — it proves each finding and drops anything it cannot prove.

It covers the codebase (attack-surface map, untrusted input traced to SQL/shell/template/path/deserialization/contract sinks, secrets in the working tree and git history, dependency CVEs reachable from your surface, OWASP) AND the AI-agent layer that generic audits miss: tool and MCP permissions, instruction/data separation (prompt injection), spend caps enforced in code rather than the prompt, wallet key exposure, and human gates.

Output is a fixed report: Findings (proven only, each with path, proof, impact, diff-style fix and a regression test) and Hardening (unproven but worth doing). Zero false positives in Findings is a rule, not a hope.

Read-only by default, never runs exploits against production, and never installs anything silently.
use_cases: Audit a repo before release or before a pentest
Review a PR that touches auth, payments or file handling
Trace untrusted input to a dangerous sink and prove exploitability
Find leaked secrets in the working tree and git history
Audit the AI agent that runs against your code
